TR-3B "Locust" / Astra: Described as a large, triangular, multi-role vehicle (aircraft and near-Earth spacecraft) developed jointly by U.S. military and corporations. It's said to operate from the secretive S-4 facility (near Papoose Lake, adjacent to Area 51/Groom Lake). Capabilities include extreme maneuvers, anti-gravity-like propulsion (via mercury plasma or similar exotic tech), and sizes up to hundreds of feet across.

Edgar Fouche's Connection: Fouche, a former aerospace engineer/contractor who claimed work at Area 51/S-4 in the 1980s–1990s, publicly described the TR-3B (or "Locust") in 1998 as the most classified U.S. vehicle, built in the late 1980s under black programs (possibly tied to SDI/Star Wars funding). He alleged it used anti-gravity/MFD (Magnetic Field Disruptor) tech for silent hovering and high-G performance, with a 600-foot-wide variant. DeLonge's account aligns closely with Fouche's details (e.g., location at S-4, massive size, triangular shape).

Russian Angle and "Extraterrestrials": In Sekret Machines, some "UFO" incidents (including abductions) are portrayed as human operations—e.g., a staged abduction in Siberia by Russians using advanced arrow/triangular craft mimicking the Locust's performance. Other events involve Russian vehicles interfering with U.S. nuclear sites to demonstrate superiority (deactivating nukes). This suggests many "alien" encounters are actually covert human tech from rival programs, not extraterrestrials.
